How It Works

How Professional Government Cleaning Works

Our government cleaning process follows a systematic, six-step protocol designed to maximize pathogen elimination and provide verifiable documentation of results. Every step is performed by trained, background-checked technicians.

1
Security Clearance and Onboarding

All cleaning personnel undergo comprehensive background checks (criminal history, sex offender registry, drug screening) before assignment. Staff receive photo identification badges and training on facility-specific security protocols, access zones, and incident reporting procedures.

2
Public Area Maintenance

Lobbies, courtrooms, public service counters, waiting areas, and hallways receive continuous daytime maintenance through day porter services and thorough after-hours deep cleaning. Public restrooms are monitored every 60-90 minutes during business hours with full cleaning after hours.

3
Office and Administrative Cleaning

Government offices receive daily janitorial service including trash removal, surface disinfection, floor care, and restroom maintenance — performed to GSA Level 2 or Level 3 standards depending on area classification and contract specifications.

4
Secure Area Protocols

Areas with classified materials, server rooms, evidence storage, or restricted access receive cleaning only during authorized windows with escorted access where required. Staff are trained on document handling protocols — found documents are reported, never moved or read.

5
QASP Compliance

Our cleaning operations are designed to pass government Quality Assurance Surveillance Plans. JaniTrack documentation provides the inspection-ready evidence that government contract administrators require — timestamped photos, task completion records, and quality scoring data.

6
Certified Payroll and Reporting

For contracts subject to the Service Contract Act or state prevailing wage laws, we provide compliant certified payroll reports, maintain accurate time records by classification, and ensure all fringe benefit payments meet DOL requirements.

FAQ

Government Cleaning FAQ — West Hartford, CT

Common questions about government cleaning services in West Hartford.

What is government building cleaning?+
Government building cleaning is professional janitorial service for federal, state, and municipal facilities that operates under a framework of GSA quality standards, security clearance requirements, prevailing wage compliance, diversity procurement goals, and formal quality assurance surveillance plans. It differs from private-sector cleaning in its regulatory complexity, documentation requirements, and the security protocols required for personnel access.
Is GreenPoint certified for government contracts?+
Yes. GreenPoint is MBE/MWBE certified through NYC SBS and New York State, registered on SAM.gov with a valid CAGE code and UEI, and NYC DOE Approved Vendor. We meet all federal, state, and municipal diversity procurement requirements and have extensive experience with government procurement processes including RFP responses, Best Value evaluations, and set-aside contract qualifications.
Are your employees background-checked for government facilities?+
Yes. All GreenPoint employees undergo comprehensive background checks including criminal history, sex offender registry, drug screening, and reference verification before assignment to any government facility. For federal buildings requiring NACI or similar investigations, we coordinate the process and ensure compliance with agency-specific requirements. Staff receive photo identification badges and facility-specific security training.
Do you comply with prevailing wage requirements?+
Yes. For contracts subject to the federal Service Contract Act or state prevailing wage laws, we pay all required wage rates and fringe benefits as determined by the Department of Labor. We provide compliant certified payroll reports, maintain accurate time records by classification, and ensure all fringe benefit payments meet regulatory requirements. Our pricing transparently reflects prevailing wage costs.
How do you handle QASP inspections?+
Our JaniTrack system is designed to produce QASP-ready documentation. Every cleaning event is recorded with timestamped photos, task completion checklists, and quality scoring — providing contract administrators with the objective evidence they need for surveillance plan evaluations. We also conduct internal quality audits using ISSA appearance level scoring to identify and correct deficiencies before government inspectors find them.
How much does government building cleaning cost?+
Government cleaning typically ranges from $0.07-$0.15 per square foot per cleaning visit for standard office areas, with prevailing wage requirements adding 30-60% compared to private-sector pricing. Public-facing areas requiring Level 3 standards cost more per square foot than Level 2 back-office areas. We provide detailed, scope-specific proposals that transparently reflect wage requirements, security costs, and quality standards.
